VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a mildly attractive fundamental picture with solid but unspectacular trajectory. Q1 2026 showed modest YoY revenue growth of +2.9% and EPS growth of +4.3%, with the company achieving its first positive Q1 postpaid phone net additions since 2013 (55K vs. consensus loss of 81K). Operating margins improved to 21.2% and ROE reached 17%, reflecting better profitability. The company raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99 and tightened postpaid net additions to the upper half of 750K-1M range. Free cash flow generation remains strong at ~$17.7B annually, supporting a 6% dividend yield with 20 consecutive years of increases. However, the balance sheet carries substantial leverage (~$120B debt) with interest expense rising 18.9% YoY to $1.94B, and the Frontier acquisition added complexity. Valuation is attractive at 10.6x P/E versus a 12-month range of 10.6-21.2x, placing it near the bottom of its historical range. The stock has declined 12.3% over the past quarter, creating a potential entry point. Near-term catalysts are limited beyond the recently declared dividend and ongoing execution of the subscriber growth strategy, though rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.47%) create a headwind for yield-oriented equities.

Verizon delivered adjusted earnings of $1.28 per share in the first quarter of 2026, up 7.6% year over year and ahead of the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.22 by 4.9%. Total operating revenue rose 2.9% from the year-ago quarter to $34.44 billion but missed the consensus mark of $35.03 billion by 1.7%
VZ posted total postpaid phone net additions of 55,000 in the quarter, its first positive first-quarter result since 2013
Interest expense rose 18.9% to $1.94 billion, a notable headwind versus the year-ago quarter

For 2026, Verizon continues to project total mobility and broadband service revenue growth of 2.0%-3.0%, cash flow from operations of $37.5-$38.0 billion, capital expenditures of $16.0-$16.5 billion, and free cash flow of $21.5 billion or more
The company now expects full-year adjusted profit between $4.95 and $4.99 per share, up from its prior range
Over the last 12 months, the company generated about 17.7 billion USD in free cash flow
Verizon entered 2025 with roughly $120 billion in debt
